# -json prints one JSON line per candidate loop: file, line, func, whether it
# was vectorized, and (if not) why. Files with a build constraint and loops
# with no indexed-assignment body at all are skipped entirely.

loopvec -json .
cmpenv stdout stdout.want

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

func AddFloat32s(dst, a, b []float32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}

func Stride(dst, a []float32) {
	for i := 1; i < len(dst); i += 2 {
		dst[i] = a[i]
	}
}

type T struct{}

func (T) Neg(dst, src []float32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = -src[i]
	}
}

func NoLoop(x int) int {
	return x + 1
}
-- guarded.go --
//go:build !goexperiment.simd

package test

func Guarded(dst, a []float32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = a[i]
	}
}
-- stdout.want --
{"file":"$WORK/ops.go","line":4,"func":"AddFloat32s","vectorized":true}
{"file":"$WORK/ops.go","line":10,"func":"Stride","vectorized":false,"reason":"loop clauses (start, step, direction, or bound) do not match a supported shape"}
{"file":"$WORK/ops.go","line":18,"func":"Neg","vectorized":false,"reason":"loops inside methods are skipped without -methods"}
